chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who slaughtered an animal but did not know whether to face it towards the Qiblah. He said, 'Eat from it.' I said to him, 'But he did not face it (towards the Qiblah).' He said, 'Do not eat from it, and do not eat from any slaughtered animal unless the name of Allah is mentioned upon it.' And he (peace be upon him) said, 'When you intend to slaughter, face the Qiblah with your slaughtered animal.'

key_terms.يُذْكَرِ اِسْمُ اَللّهِ: the name of Allah is mentioned (dhikr)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on slaughtering an animal without facing the Qiblah or reciting Allah's name?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) distinguishes between the recommended act of facing the Qiblah during slaughter and the essential condition of reciting Allah's name. He clarifies that while facing the Qiblah is a recommended practice for the slaughterer, the meat remains permissible if the Qiblah is forgotten, but becomes impermissible if the name of Allah is not mentioned, highlighting the primacy of the *dhikr* in establishing halal status.
